title: Analyze Graphs of Relationships Between Two Variables
objective: I can use a table and a graph to determine and analyze the relationship between two variable quantities.
model: table to coordinate graph: each row becomes an ordered pair with the independent variable first; read a point in context; rate of change

widgets.component: independent/dependent review (songs at $2, calories burned, plant height, what the independent variable is)
widgets.root: Identical to the config warm-up and a fair 9-1 review; keys verified.

widgets.component: tickets at $45, tram at 1,200 ft per min, 48 km per hour, simple interest $26.25, hose rates, rate of change 6 liters per hour, why (0, 0) is on the graph
widgets.root: Keys recomputed (135, 3,600, 96, 18,000, 6,000, (5, 6000), 48, 26.25, (6, 48), 18 more liters, 63, 45, 6 liters per hour). The Nakai simple-interest and Sandia tram contexts come from the lesson's own Connect, so they are in scope. Challenge 4.4 uses 'steeper' informally and no slope term.

widgets.component: 'Which ordered pair belongs on the ticket graph for 2 tickets?', 'Why is the line on the football ticket graph dashed?', 'Using the ticket table, what are the coordinates for 4 tickets?', 'On Nakai's graph, which variable is on the x-axis?'
widgets.root: Every one of these questions is about a graph or table (the ticket graph, the ticket table, Nakai's graph) that is never drawn: the items carry no viz. 3.4, 3.5, 3.6 and 5.1 cannot be answered from the stem, and 2.2/2.3/3.6 do not even state the $45 price. The studio gate only checks stems that say 'the graph shows', so these slipped through.
widgets.replacement: Attach figures: a coord viz of (0,0), (1,45), (2,90), (3,135), (4,180), (5,225) with axes 'Number of tickets' and 'Total cost ($)' and a dashed connector to 2.2, 2.3, 3.4, 3.5, 5.2; the same six rows as a table viz to 3.6; and a coord viz of years against interest earned (0,0), (1,26.25), (2,52.50), (3,78.75) to 5.1, with the $750, 3.5% context in one stem sentence. State '$45 per ticket' in 2.2, 2.3 and 3.6.

widgets.component: 'Football tickets cost $45 each, so the graph follows c = 45t. Sort each ordered pair: on the ticket graph or not?'
widgets.root: States the relationship as the letter equation c = 45t with c and t undefined. Writing and defining a two-variable equation is 9-3's objective (9-2's canon says 'cost = 45 × tickets'). The task itself (test an ordered pair against a rule) is on objective.
widgets.replacement: Keep the cards ((1, 45), (2, 90), (4, 180) on; (3, 120), (2, 100), (5, 200) off) and replace the stem with 'Tickets cost $45 each, so the total cost is 45 times the number of tickets. Sort each ordered pair (tickets, total cost): is it on the ticket graph?' and show the table viz beside it.

widgets.component: coordinate graph, 'as the number of laps goes up, what happens to the distance?'
widgets.root: Rendered the coord viz: points are right, axes labelled, key right (it goes up; flat when the series is constant).

widgets.component: read a value off the graph, find an ordered pair, but also 'Which equation matches the graph?' (y = x + 6, s = 12.5w, d = 6.5l)
widgets.root: Equation-from-graph is the objective of 9-3 and uses y = kx and y = x + c before they are taught. In sampled seeds 1 of 6 L2 slots, 3 of 6 L3 slots and 1 of 6 L4 slots are 'Which equation matches the graph?'. The pair items (1, 13) and extrapolation items are fine.
widgets.replacement: Delete the 'Which equation matches the graph?' templates from graphRelationship. Replace them with 'Which table matches the graph?' (four small table viz) at L2, 'What is the rate of change shown by the graph?' at L3, and 'Which ordered pair is NOT on the graph?' at L4. Also change the L4 apples template (2.5 apples per bag gives 37.5 apples) to a continuous quantity such as kilograms.

widgets.component: 'A taxi charges $3 for each mile. The rule is c = 3m. Work out each c and plot (m, c)' on a coordinate plane
widgets.root: The plotting task is the lesson's model and is right, but the rule is stated as a letter equation (c = 3m, a = b + 4, t = f + 5) that 9-3 teaches; 9-2's own Explore speaks in words ('cost = 45 × tickets').
widgets.replacement: In plot.js mkTable (and mkRatio), print the rule in words ('The cost is 3 times the number of miles', 'Ana's age is 4 more than her brother's') and keep the letters only as the axis names; nothing else changes.

widgets.component: 'The ratio of sundaes to ounces of sauce is 2 : 3. Plot each pair from the table'
widgets.root: Table-to-points plotting with the first quantity on the x-axis and a swapped-axes miss; ratio wording is the grade 6 predecessor of the same steady-rate relationship, no new formula.
Directly traps the swapped-coordinates error, which is the main 9-2 misconception.

widgets.component: coordinates swapped, additive rule instead of multiplicative, grid lines worth 5 read as 1
widgets.root: Error step indices match the faulty lines; table cells (0, 24, 60, 7) correct.

formulaOrder.formula: letter equation as the rule of a relationship (c = 45t, c = 3m, a = b + 4)
choosing an equation that matches a graph (y = kx, y = x + c)

typography: twoVarTable / graphRelationship / twoVarProblem stems print 'the Ana\'s age', 'the today\'s temperature', 'the yesterday\'s temperature', 'The Leo\'s score', 'the Mia\'s score' (a possessive after 'the'), which reads as broken English to a student (Practice 4.3-4.6, Challenge 1.1-1.6)
graphRelationship L4 asks for 37.5 apples; a count of apples cannot be fractional
